title: paged-kv-cache: block allocator reuse, pinning, and TTL-based soft eviction
author: Liam Chen
description: Motivation: reduce GC/allocator churn and tail latency in the paged KV cache under high-concurrency continuous-batching workloads. This change implements allocator reuse across allocation windows, introduces an explicit pinning API for hot keys to avoid premature eviction during long-running requests, and adds a TTL-based soft-eviction path to make space under pressure without aggressive compaction. Scope: (1) Rework paged block allocator to maintain per-NUMA free lists and a global reuse pool with lock-free fast-path allocations where possible. (2) Add pinning semantics to block manager so callers (runtime/gateways) can mark KV entries as pinned for the duration of an inference trace; pinned blocks are exempt from normal eviction heuristics. (3) TTL soft-eviction path: entries with expired TTL are preferred for reuse but are only reclaimed when not pinned; when pressure is high a background compactor converts soft-evictions into reclaimed blocks. (4) Heuristic changes: favor reuse of recently-freed blocks that match size/stride to improve cache locality and reduce fragmentation. (5) Add metrics (kv.blocks.reused, kv.blocks.pinned, kv.blocks.compacted, kv.pinning.latency) and feature-flag to toggle new behavior at runtime. Checklist: - [x] Allocator reuse fast-path implementation - [x] Pin/unpin APIs + runtime integration - [x] TTL soft-eviction and background compactor - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] Microbenchmarks and perf numbers - [x] Docs for operators and rollout notes. Rollout plan: feature toggled off by default on main, enabled in canary and perf-canary for 48h, then gradual ramp to 50% traffic; monitor kv.* metrics and tail latency. Backout plan: flip feature flag off (no schema change), compactor idempotent so turning off immediately stops reuse path. Related work: ENG-5121 (KV cache perf), ENG-4987 (continuous batching SLO), SUP-134 (customer incident that motivated pinning).
commits: 3 commits: (a) initial block-allocator: per-NUMA freelists + reuse pool; (b) add pin/unpin API, TTL soft-evict + compactor; (c) tests, metrics, docs, and CI fixes
ci_status: passed (initial: lint fail -> fixed with formatting; second run: all checks passed; integration tests passed in canary)
review_comments: Priya: requested metrics and asked for compaction safety when pinned entries exist; addressed by adding kv.blocks.compacted and extra safety checks. Marco: suggested using a size-classed free-list to reduce fragmentation; implemented lightweight matching heuristic. Jenna: noted potential regression on long traces; added additional integration test and small stress harness. After addressing comments all reviewers approved and requested a perf-canary run before full rollout.
benchmark_results: Microbench on 4xA100 equivalent setup: throughput +6-12% across common batch sizes (1-8) for chat workloads; p99 token latency down 8-15% under 75th percentile load; memory fragmentation reduced ~18% in steady state. Bench scripts and raw data attached to the PR artifacts.
release_notes: Improves paged KV cache allocator reuse, adds pinning to avoid eviction of in-use entries, and introduces TTL-based soft eviction and compaction; expected throughput and tail latency improvements for continuous-batching workloads. Feature gated - requires rollout and monitoring.
